title: Pressure-cooker poached salmon
subtitle: Silky, evenly cooked salmon in 3 minutes
excerpt: Salmon fillets steam-poached under pressure in 3 minutes. The sealed environment cooks the fish gently and evenly from all sides, producing a moist, flaky result without the risk of overcooking.
sourceNotes: Poaching fish in a flavoured liquid is a traditional French and British technique documented in Escoffier and Mrs Beeton. The pressure-cooker steam-poaching method was popularised in electric pressure cooker recipe communities in the 2010s and produces a particularly gentle result.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Poached salmon is excellent served cold. Cook ahead and refrigerate for up to 2 days for salads and sandwiches.

content.text: Pressure-cooker poached salmon cooks in 3 minutes at low pressure and produces a result that is difficult to overcook. The sealed, steamy environment distributes heat evenly around each fillet, so the fish cooks gently from all sides rather than only from below. The result is moist, silky, and fully cooked, the opposite of the dry, chalky salmon that comes from an oven that ran too hot.

Use low pressure if your cooker has a low setting, fish cooks very quickly and the gentler pressure produces a better texture. If your cooker only has high pressure, reduce the cook time to 2 minutes.

Flavour the poaching liquid to season the fish from the outside as it cooks. Lemon, bay, peppercorns, and dill are the classic combination, simple, clean, and complementary to the natural richness of salmon.

items.prepNote: about 150 g each, skin on or off

content.text: Add 300 ml of cold water to the pressure cooker with the lemon slices, bay leaves, peppercorns, and salt. Place the trivet inside. Lay the salmon fillets on the trivet, not touching each other if possible. Seal the lid and bring to low pressure. Cook at low pressure for 3 minutes, or high pressure for 2 minutes. Quick-release immediately.

Open the lid and check the salmon, it should be opaque throughout, flaking easily at the thickest point. If the centre is still translucent, seal the lid and cook at low pressure for 1 more minute. Serve immediately with the poaching liquid as a light sauce, or allow to cool and serve at room temperature.

rows.symptom: The salmon is overcooked and dry
rows.cause: High pressure was used for 3 minutes, or the fillets were thin.
rows.fix: For fillets under 2 cm thick, reduce to 2 minutes at low pressure or 1 minute at high pressure. Quick-release is essential, do not allow the fish to sit in the hot pot after opening.

rows.cause: The fillets were thick, or low pressure was slightly under-achieved.
rows.fix: Add 1 minute at low pressure. Salmon fillets over 3 cm thick at the centre may need 4 minutes.

content.text: Poached salmon is a useful technique to have in the repertoire. It serves dinner warm with new potatoes and greens, provides cold salmon for salads and sandwiches the next day, and forms the base for kedgeree or fish cakes later in the week. The pressure cooker version is faster than the stovetop method and produces a more consistently moist result.
